provenance.note: Each commitment cites a dated official record: GVMC's and the state's own filings to the NGT, APPCB's reports to it, the AP High Court's orders recording GVMC's dates, or MoHUA's AMRUT 2.0 lists. The draft Green City Action Plan GVMC posted for public comment on 19 Oct 2024 is cited only for context and dated status records; a draft is not a commitment, so its 2034 water-loss target has no row. AMRUT milestones checked against MoHUA's live list on 2026-10-14.

headline: What Visakhapatnam has promised about its water and sewage, and by when
intro: Most of the city's dated promises are about sewage: how much of the city is connected, how much is treated, and when the rest will be. They come from GVMC's and the state's own filings to the National Green Tribunal, the AP High Court's orders, and the national AMRUT 2.0 project lists. Where several documents date the same work, it has one row and every date is in its history. From the AMRUT 2.0 list the register carries every GVMC project of Rs 10 crore or more, and every project past its scheduled date that is not marked complete.

status_legend.delivered: The promised thing verifiably happened, even if late. The dates show how late.
status_legend.on-track: The stated date has not passed and a dated progress figure for the work is consistent with it.
status_legend.slipped: The institution itself has moved the date and the latest date has not passed. Old and new dates are both shown.
status_legend.overdue: The latest stated date, original or revised, has passed and we have not found a dated record of completion.
status_legend.stalled: Work or approvals have stopped, by the institution's own account or a court's.
status_legend.unverified: We can cite the promise but cannot yet cite its current status either way.

update_model: History is kept, never overwritten. A status changes only against a dated citation.
sources_note: GVMC's own notes, affidavits and reports to the National Green Tribunal and the High Court's committee (2021 to 2025), the Government of Andhra Pradesh's compliance affidavit (February 2026) and its monthly progress report for February 2024, APPCB's report to the Tribunal of 27 April 2026, the AP High Court's orders of 12 November 2025 and 11 March 2026, and MoHUA's AMRUT 2.0 lists. The draft Green City Action Plan (IFC for GVMC), posted by GVMC for comment on 19 Oct 2024, is cited for context only. Press reports are not used.

commitments.title: Pendurthi underground drainage network
commitments.what: Complete the underground drainage network for the Pendurthi area (Zone VIII), which GVMC put at Rs 362 crore in its 2021 filings to the National Green Tribunal. GVMC's notes of November 2023 and December 2025 give the Pendurthi package as Rs 412 crore, and the draft Green City Action Plan (p78) describes that Rs 412 crore as a 226 km network and a 46 MLD tertiary treatment plant with 15 years of upkeep; we have not found a document that reconciles the two figures. The new Narava plant this network feeds and the state's target for sewer connections in Gajuwaka and Pendurthi by FY 2028-29 are separate rows.

commitments.title: A new 54 MLD treatment plant at Narava
commitments.what: Bring into use a new 54 MLD sewage treatment plant beside the existing one at Narava. GVMC says the Pendurthi and Gajuwaka sewer networks, which are separate rows, will carry sewage to it. In 2021 GVMC told the Tribunal the plant would be completed by the end of October 2021, then that it would be 'commenced by the end of August 2022'. The state's list of plants for February 2024 shows a second 54 MLD plant at Narava commissioned in October 2022, with 15 MLD of its capacity in use. GVMC's notes of November 2023 and December 2025 list the plant as in execution, due by December 2024 and then December 2026. Every date is shown below.

commitments.title: Second 25 MLD treatment plant at Appughar, with new sewer lines
commitments.what: Build a second 25 MLD sewage treatment plant beside the existing one at Appughar, with additional sewer lines and gaps in the existing network filled, part funded by AMRUT 2.0. GVMC's December 2025 note says the plant is to treat dry-weather flow from drains that now reach the sea. The documents give five costs: Rs 88 crore (GVMC, 2023), Rs 90 crore with drain diversions (GVMC's 2024 affidavit; the draft Green City Action Plan), Rs 372 crore (GVMC, December 2025), Rs 363.38 crore (AMRUT 2.0 project AP-GVMC-4780) and a Rs 272 crore contract (High Court, March 2026). Reading AP-GVMC-4780 as this work is an inference from its title, its AMRUT funding, its contract stage and the state's AMRUT 2.0 listing of a 25 MLD GVMC plant with the same March 2028 date; we have not found a document that states the link.

commitment_source.label: GVMC note of 27.11.2023 to the High Court's committee in WP(PIL) 248/2020, annexed to CPCB's reply in NGT OA 240/2025 (SZ), PDF pp40-43

status_history.note: 'Providing additional Sewer Network & Gaps including construction of 25 MLD STP at Appughar': 50 km, Rs 88 crore, 'Tender Stage', probable completion 'Mar'2026 (2 years duration)', 25% of the funds proposed under AMRUT 2.0 and 75% from GVMC (PDF p43).
status_history.source_label: GVMC note of 27.11.2023 to the High Court's committee in WP(PIL) 248/2020, annexed to CPCB's reply in NGT OA 240/2025 (SZ), PDF pp40-43

status_history.note: GVMC's sworn affidavit counts a 25 MLD plant inside Rs 641 crore of new sewerage works, 80% from its own funds, to start in May-June 2024 and finish 'by the Dec'2027' (PDF p5); its 2023 note splits that Rs 641 crore into this project (Rs 88 crore) and Madhurawada (Rs 553 crore). The affidavit also lists the remaining 14 of 24 drains that reach the sea, with gaps in the sewer network and house connections, at Rs 90 crore, 'In tenders', with 'Construction of New STP Mar'2026 (2 years duration)' (PDF p7); it does not name the site.
status_history.source_label: GVMC Commissioner's affidavit, NGT OA 40/2024 (SZ)

status_history.note: The draft plan lists 'Diversion of dry weather flow drains and streams, which includes gaps in the sewerage network, house service connections and construction of an additional 25MLD STP at Appughar with a cost of INR 90 crore' as 'Sanctioned and Under Tender Stage' (p78), naming the site of the affidavit's Rs 90 crore line.
status_history.source_label: Draft Visakhapatnam Green City Action Plan (IFC for GVMC, dated Sept 2024), posted by GVMC for comment on 19 Oct 2024

status_history.note: The High Court records the Advocate General's statement that tendering for the second Appughar plant would be completed by December 2025, construction would start around January 2026, and the plant would take about 18 months to build.

status_history.note: GVMC now gives the project as 207 km of sewer network with the 25 MLD plant, Rs 372 crore, 'Tender Stage', probable completion 'Mar'2029' (PDF p25). The Rs 641 crore plan is restated as Rs 925 crore, now 25 MLD here and 20 MLD in Madhurawada, to start in Feb-Mar 2026 and finish 'by the Mar'2029'; the note's text also puts the two new projects at 'Rs.887(553+334) crores' (PDF p24).

status_history.note: The state lists 25 MLD and 20 MLD of new treatment capacity for the city by March 2029, the sizes GVMC gives for Appughar and Madhurawada, against a gap of 69 MLD between sewage generated (248 MLD, PDF p71) and the 179 MLD of plant capacity in use; installed capacity is 237 MLD (PDF p78). GVMC gave it as 450 km with a 50 MLD plant in 2023 and as 398 km with a 20 MLD first-phase plant in December 2025, at Rs 553 crore both times.
